facts.raw_span: 54-year-old woman
history of stage III invasive ductal breast carcinoma
treated with mastectomy and chemoradiation 4 years earlier
urinary frequency
worsening right-sided pelvic pain
weight loss
MRI of the pelvis showed multiple fibroids and a heterogeneous 9.4 cm lesion involving the right uterine fundus/cornua
intraoperatively, the mass was found in the right retroperitoneal space, tracking along the broad ligament and encasing the right external iliac artery
grossly, the specimen was a detached, fragmented, ill-defined mass (14 × 12 × 4 cm) with fleshy solid and cystic components, central hemorrhage, and necrosis

microscopically, the tumor invaded from the serosal surface into the myometrium and comprised sheets of small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitoses (32 per 10 high-power fields), pseudo-rosette formation, foci of cytoplasmic clearing, and necrosis
immunohistochemical stains showed diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1
immunohistochemical stains showed negativity for keratin, DOG1, synaptophysin, desmin, myogenin, WT-1, CD45, inhibin, GATA-3, and SOX-10

microscopically, the tumor invaded from the serosal surface into the myometrium and comprised sheets of small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitoses (32 per 10 high-power fields), pseudo-rosette formation, foci of cytoplasmic clearing, and necrosis
immunohistochemical stains showed diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1

concepts.why: The tumor's microscopic features, including small, round hyperchromatic cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, frequent mitoses, and pseudo-rosette formation, are consistent with Ewing's Sarcoma, and the immunohistochemical stains showing diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1 support this diagnosis.
The presence of a large, heterogeneous mass in the right uterine fundus/cornua, with features of necrosis and high mitotic activity, is consistent with a diagnosis of Uterine Leiomyosarcoma.

The patient's history of stage III invasive ductal breast carcinoma, treated with mastectomy and chemoradiation 4 years earlier, increases the likelihood of metastatic disease, and the presence of a large mass in the right uterine fundus/cornua could represent a metastasis.

The tumor's undifferentiated features, including a lack of specific immunohistochemical staining, and the presence of a large, heterogeneous mass in the right uterine fundus/cornua, are consistent with a diagnosis of Undifferentiated Uterine Sarcoma.

rationales.F10: The microscopic description of the tumor is highly suggestive of Ewing's Sarcoma, with features such as small, round hyperchromatic cells, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, and pseudo-rosette formation.
rationales.F11: The immunohistochemical stains showing diffuse positivity for CD99, KIT, and cyclin D1 are characteristic of Ewing's Sarcoma.
rationales.F12: The absence of staining for keratin, DOG1, synaptophysin, desmin, myogenin, WT-1, CD45, inhibin, GATA-3, and SOX-10 helps to rule out other tumor types, such as Uterine Leiomyosarcoma and Metastatic Breast Cancer.
